info.title: InvoicePDFs
info.description:
InvoicePDFs turns a JSON document into a polished PDF — invoices, credit notes, quotes, receipts, proformas, purchase orders and delivery notes. The API validates your data, computes totals correctly (tax, discounts, shipping), and returns a downloadable, professional PDF.

This package is the official client for the InvoicePDFs API, generated from the OpenAPI specification.

Documentation: https://invoicepdfs.com

get.description:
Is the API process alive.

Answers as long as the process can serve a request; it checks nothing
behind it. For whether the service can actually do work, use
`get_readiness`.
Which build is deployed.

Can the API serve real traffic — dependencies included.

Checks the database, storage, and the separate render service, and reports
each one. `status` is `ready` only when all three are `ok`, so this is the
check to point a load balancer at. `get_health` answers sooner but proves
less.

The account behind the current credential, and the plan it is on.

Works with either an API key or a Firebase token, so it is the cheapest
way to confirm a credential is live and see what it can reach.

patch.description: Update the authenticated account's name or email.

post.description:
Register a new account using a Firebase ID token.

The client authenticates with Firebase (email/password, Google, etc.)
and sends the resulting ID token here to create an InvoicePDFs account.

Exchange a Firebase ID token for account info.

Use this on login: the client authenticates with Firebase, sends the ID
token here, and receives the InvoicePDFs account details. The Firebase
token itself is used as the Bearer token for subsequent API calls.
Revoke all Firebase refresh tokens for the authenticated user.
Exchange a Firebase refresh token for a new ID token.
Send a password reset email via Firebase.
Confirm a password reset using the code from the reset email.

get.description:
Every API key on the account, including revoked ones.

Shows only the last four characters: the key itself is stored hashed and
cannot be recovered.

post.description:
Create an API key and return it once.

The response is the only place the key appears — it is stored hashed, so a
lost key cannot be recovered, only replaced.

Keys are not scoped: any key can do anything this account can, including
creating further keys and deleting data. Treat one as a full credential.

delete.description:
Stop an API key working, permanently.

Takes effect immediately and cannot be undone — issue a new key with
`create_api_key` instead. The record is kept, so the key still appears in
`list_api_keys` with a revoked date and the audit log stays readable.

Revoking an already-revoked key succeeds and changes nothing.

get.description: One API key's details by id, without the key itself.

patch.description:
Rename an API key.

The key itself is unchanged and keeps working. To replace the secret while
keeping the record, use `rotate_api_key`.

post.description: Revoke the existing key and create a new one with the same name.

get.description:
The identities you issue documents *as*, newest first.

One per entity you bill from — a business with two trading names or two tax
registrations needs two. For how documents *look* rather than who issues
them, see the branding profiles.

post.description:
Create an identity to issue documents as: the seller side.

`legal_name`, `tax_id`, address and bank details are what appears as the
issuer, and what an e-invoicing ruleset checks. Distinct from a branding
profile, which sets colours and a logo and says nothing about who you are.

get.description: One business profile.

patch.description:
Change a business profile.

Only the fields you send are changed. Documents already issued keep the
issuer details they carried at the time.

delete.description:
Remove a business profile.

`409` if any document was issued under it, naming what still points at it.

409.description: The profile is named on documents or recurring invoices. `details.referenced_by` counts each one.

get.description:
The looks a document can be rendered in, newest first.

Colours, logo, fonts and footer text — how a document appears. Who it is
issued by is a business profile, which is a different thing.

post.description:
Create a look: colours, logo, fonts and footer.

Applies on top of whichever template a render names, so one template can
serve several brands. Mark one as the default and documents that name no
profile will use it.

get.description: One branding profile.

patch.description:
Change a branding profile.

Only the fields you send are changed. `hide_invoicepdfs_branding` is stored
on any plan but only honoured on a plan that includes it — it is applied
when a document renders, not validated here, so setting it on a plan without
it is accepted and has no effect.

delete.description:
Remove a branding profile.

Deleting the default is allowed: the oldest remaining profile becomes the
default in its place, so documents that name no profile keep rendering.

post.description:
Make this the profile used when a document names none.

Exactly one profile is the default; setting a new one clears the previous.

Attach a logo image to this branding profile.

Replaces whatever logo the profile carried. The image is embedded when a
document renders, so a later change applies to future renders and leaves
PDFs already produced as they were.

delete.description: Remove this profile's logo, leaving its colours and text intact.

get.description:
The people and companies you bill, newest first.

Cursor-paginated. A customer is optional — the stateless render endpoints take
a buyer inline — but storing one lets a document reference it by id.

post.description:
Store a customer you can bill repeatedly.

`tax_id` and `electronic_address` are what e-invoicing needs: a buyer VAT
number and the Peppol identifier a receiver is addressed by. Neither is
required for a plain PDF.

get.description: One stored customer.

patch.description:
Change a stored customer.

Only the fields you send are changed — omit one to leave it alone, send
`null` to clear it. Documents already issued keep the details they were
issued with; this does not rewrite them.

delete.description:
Remove a customer.

`409` if any document still references them, naming what does. History is
kept rather than rewritten.

409.description: The customer is named on documents or recurring invoices. `details.referenced_by` counts each one.

get.description:
Every document on the account, newest first.

Cursor-paginated: pass the `next_cursor` from a response to fetch the page
after it. Filter by `document_type` or `status` to narrow the list.

post.description:
Create a document in `draft`.

Totals are computed and stored at creation, so the figures you read back are
the ones that were issued rather than a recalculation. Nothing is rendered —
use `create_document_render` once the document is final.

get.description: One document, with the totals stored when it was created.

patch.description:
Change a document that is still a `draft`.

A finalized document is a record of what was issued and cannot be edited;
`409` if it has moved past `draft`. Only the fields you send are changed —
omit one to leave it alone, and send `null` to clear it.

delete.description:
Permanently remove a `draft`.

`409` if anything still points at it — a render, a delivery or a payment —
naming what does. Finalized documents are voided or archived, not deleted.

409.description: The document is not a draft. Only drafts can be deleted.

post.description:
Copy a document into a new `draft`.

The copy gets the next available number rather than the original's, so it can
be finalized without colliding with the document it came from.

Issue a `draft`: fix its number and totals.

From here the document is a record. It can be sent, marked paid, voided or
archived, but not edited — `update_document` returns `409` afterwards.

Cancel a document that was issued.

Voiding is how a finalized document is withdrawn, since it cannot be deleted.
The PDF renders with a `VOID` mark from then on, so a copy already sent is
distinguishable from the live one.

Record that the document reached the customer.

**This does not send anything** — it only moves the status, for when the
document was delivered by some means of your own. Use `send_document` to
have us email it.
Record that the document was paid in full.

Undo `mark_paid`, returning the document to `sent`.

For a payment that was recorded in error or later reversed.
Bring an archived document back to `finalized`.

Render a stored document to a PDF.

Use this when the document lives here. To render one you hold yourself,
without storing it, use `render_document`.

The response carries a signed `download_url` that needs no API key, valid
until `expires_at`.

Queue the document to be emailed, with its PDF attached.

The document must be finalized; sending a draft is a 409. `attach_pdf`
defaults to true, and on that path a render must already exist — the email
attaches an existing render rather than making one — so the natural
sequence is create, finalize, render, send, and sending straight after
finalizing is refused with `No render exists for this document`. Send with
`attach_pdf: false` and no render is needed, because none is attached.

Returns 202 with the delivery in `queued`. The mail is sent in the
background and retried on transient failure; poll `GET /deliveries/{id}`
for the outcome.

get.description:
Every email delivery attempted for this document.

One row per attempt, newest first, including the ones that failed — which is
where to look when a customer says the invoice never arrived.

post.description:
Check that a document body is well-formed, without pricing it.

The cheapest of the three stateless operations: no totals are computed and no
PDF is produced. Use `calculate_document` for the money and `render_document`
for the document.

Compute the totals for a document without storing or rendering it.

Returns the same breakdown — subtotal, discounts, tax, shipping, total — that
a render would print, so a checkout page can show a figure before committing
to one.

Render a document supplied inline, storing nothing but the PDF.

The stateless path: pass the whole document in the body and get a PDF back,
with no customer, business profile or stored document required. To render a
document that already lives here, use `create_document_render`.

Returns JSON with a signed `download_url` by default. Ask for the bytes
directly with `output.delivery: "binary"` or `Accept: application/pdf`.

200.description: The rendered document. Returns the PDF itself instead when `output.delivery` is `binary` or the request sends `Accept: application/pdf`.

202.description: Returned when `output.mode` is `async`: the render is queued and a worker will produce it. Follow it with `GET /renders/{render_id}`.

post.description:
Check a document against an e-invoicing ruleset without rendering it.

Costs no renders: nothing is stored and no PDF is produced, so a caller can
check every invoice they are about to send rather than discovering the
problem from a rejection weeks later.

Two tiers run, and both are reported. The mandatory-field check names a
field of the request you can go and change. Schematron then serializes the
document and runs the **published rules at a pinned version** over the
result — the same artefacts an access point runs — so a finding here quotes
the rule id a rejection notice would quote.

Read `valid` together with `fully_checked`: `valid` says nothing fatal was
found, and `rulesets` says what actually ran to find it.

The e-invoicing XML for a document, without storing anything.

Takes the same body as `/validate-compliance`, and the pairing is the point:
check first, then take the XML once it passes. Nothing here validates
against the ruleset — a document missing mandatory fields serialises to XML
missing those elements, which is a more useful artefact to look at than a
refusal, and `/validate-compliance` is where the refusal belongs.

The syntax is not a parameter. It follows from the profile, because a
profile already is a syntax plus a ruleset, and asking a caller for both is
asking them to know that Peppol means UBL.

200.description: The document as XML, in the syntax the chosen profile is expressed in — UBL for Peppol BIS, CII for Factur-X.

get.description:
The e-invoicing XML for a document already stored here.

Reads `data_json` directly rather than going through the render path's
reconstruction: the status, the logo and the source document's number are
all attached there for the *PDF*, and none of them belong in the XML. The
credit note's BG-3 reference is already in the stored payload, resolved when
the document was written.

parameters.name: profile

schema.description: Which ruleset to write this against. No default: a document valid under one can be rejected by another, so the choice is the request.
schema.title: Profile

parameters.description: Which ruleset to write this against. No default: a document valid under one can be rejected by another, so the choice is the request.

200.description: The stored document as XML, in the syntax the chosen profile is expressed in — UBL for Peppol BIS, CII for Factur-X.

get.description: Files attached to this document.

post.description:
Attach an already-uploaded file to a document.

Takes the `file_id` from `upload_file` rather than the bytes, so one upload
can be attached to several documents.

delete.description: Detach a file from this document. The file itself is kept.

get.description:
The built-in templates every account can render with.

Your own designs are listed separately by `list_custom_templates`.
One built-in template: its id, name and the options it accepts.

post.description:
Design a template of your own, starting as a `draft`.

A custom template is a built-in plus your own configuration — it does not
replace the layout, it adjusts it. Drafts can be rendered while you iterate;
publish it when you want a version pinned.

get.description: Templates this account has designed, newest first. Cursor-paginated.
One of this account's templates.

patch.description: Change a custom template. Only the fields you send are changed.

delete.description:
Remove a custom template.

`409` if a document or a recurring schedule still names it.

post.description: Copy a custom template into a new `draft`, to change without affecting the original.

Mark a custom template `published`.

`409` if it is published already. Publishing is what makes a version
pinnable, so a document rendered months from now can still be reproduced.

get.description: One built-in template: its id, name and the options it accepts.

post.description:
Render a template against sample data to see how it looks.

**This is a real render**: it counts against the monthly quota and is metered
like any other, because it does the same work. Use it to check a design, not
as a way to render documents.

parameters.name: version

schema.description: Preview the config this version recorded rather than the template's current config. Only a custom (`ctpl_`) template has versions.
schema.title: Version

parameters.description: Preview the config this version recorded rather than the template's current config. Only a custom (`ctpl_`) template has versions.

200.description: The rendered preview. Returns the PDF itself instead when `output.delivery` is `binary` or the request sends `Accept: application/pdf`.

get.description: Every published version of a custom template, newest first.

post.description:
Snapshot a template's current configuration as a new version.

A document can pin a version, so a render months later reproduces the design
that was live when it was issued rather than today's.

get.description: One version's stored configuration.

post.description:
Put a template back to the config a version recorded.

The template moves; the version does not. Restoring v1 over v3's config does
not delete v3 or renumber anything — the next snapshot is v4, and the history
stays a record of what happened rather than a record of the last decision.
Take a version first if the config being replaced is worth keeping.

get.description:
One render: its status, its totals, and how to download it.

`download_url` and `expires_at` are `null` until the render is `completed`,
and a `failed` render carries a `failure` explaining why. Poll this after an
asynchronous render.

Fetch the PDF, by signature or by API key.

Two ways in, and the signature is checked *first* — before the row is looked
up — so a forged token cannot be used to tell a real render id from an
invented one. It also means the token path costs no auth work at all, which
matters because this is the one endpoint a browser hits directly.

parameters.name: token

schema.description: The signature from this render's `download_url`. Present it and no API key is needed — that is what makes the URL a link. Omit it and the request authenticates normally.
schema.title: Token

parameters.description: The signature from this render's `download_url`. Present it and no API key is needed — that is what makes the URL a link. Omit it and the request authenticates normally.

get.description: Payments recorded against one document, newest first.

post.description:
Record a payment received against an invoice.

The currency is taken from the invoice rather than from the request, so a
payment can never disagree with what was billed.

Refused with 409 while the invoice is still a draft. Recording a payment
does not move the invoice to `paid` — use `mark_paid` for that.

get.description: One recorded payment by id.

patch.description:
Correct a payment that was already recorded.

Only the fields you send are changed. The invoice's status and totals are
left alone.

delete.description:
Remove a recorded payment.

The payment is deleted outright rather than reversed, and the invoice's
status is left alone. The deletion is kept in the audit log.

get.description: Batch jobs on this account, newest first.

post.description:
Queue many documents to be rendered at once.

Returns `202` — the batch is recorded and a worker renders it; nothing is
rendered inside this request. Poll `get_batch` for progress, then
`download_batch` for the results.

The whole batch is refused if it would exceed the monthly quota, rather than
rendering part of it.

get.description:
A batch's status and its per-item counts.

The poll surface: `total_items`, `completed_items` and `failed_items` say how
far it has got without listing every item.

Every item in a batch with its own status, newest first.

Where to look when `failed_items` is not zero: each row carries its error and,
once rendered, its `render_id`.

post.description:
Stop a batch that has not finished.

Items not yet started are cancelled. An item already rendering completes —
the work is done and cancelling it would waste it.

get.description:
Every completed render in the batch, as a ZIP.

`409` until the batch is `completed`. Items that failed are simply absent, so
check `failed_items` rather than counting files.

200.description: ZIP archive of every completed render in the batch

get.description:
One email delivery by id — an email sent to a customer.

Not to be confused with `get_webhook_delivery`, which is an HTTP POST to
one of your webhook endpoints.

post.description:
Queue a fresh delivery copying a failed one.

Returns 202 with the new delivery in `queued`. Transient failures are
already retried automatically; this is for after those are exhausted.

Set up a schedule that issues invoices on its own.

Starts `active`, so the first invoice is issued when the schedule next
falls due. The invoices it produces are ordinary documents — read them with
`list_generated_invoices`.

get.description:
The schedules on this account, newest first.

These are the recurring definitions, not the invoices they produce; for
those, use `list_generated_invoices`. Narrow with `status`.
One recurring schedule by id.

patch.description:
Change a recurring schedule.

Only the fields you send are changed. Refused with 409 once the schedule is
cancelled, which is terminal. Invoices already issued are not revisited.

delete.description:
End a schedule permanently.

Terminal: it cannot be resumed or edited afterwards, and cancelling twice
is refused with 409. To stop issuing temporarily, use
`pause_recurring_invoice` instead.

Invoices already issued are left alone.

post.description:
Stop a schedule issuing invoices, for now.

Only an `active` schedule can be paused; anything else is refused with 409.
Nothing already issued changes. Restart it with `resume_recurring_invoice`.

Start a paused schedule issuing again.

Only a `paused` schedule can be resumed; anything else is refused with 409.
A cancelled schedule cannot be brought back — create a new one.

get.description:
The invoices one schedule has actually issued, newest first.

The documents produced by this schedule, as opposed to
`list_recurring_invoices`, which lists the schedules themselves.

post.description:
Store a file and get an id for it.

Where logos and document attachments come from: upload once, then reference
the returned `file_id` from a branding profile or an attachment.

get.description: A stored file's metadata — name, type and size.

delete.description:
Remove a stored file.

`409` if a branding profile or a document attachment still references it.

get.description:
Renders used this calendar month, against the plan's quota.

The period starts at midnight UTC on the first of the month.

For rate limits, log retention and overage, use `get_usage_limits`; for
the individual renders behind the count, `list_usage_events`.

One row per metered render, newest first.

The detail behind the count `get_usage` returns, each row naming the
render that produced it.

Every ceiling on the account, and how close you are to each.

A superset of `get_usage`: the render quota and what is left of it, plus
requests per second, how long API logs are kept, and overage — whether it
is enabled and available on the plan, how many renders have gone over,
and what they have cost so far.

The cost estimate is rounded up, so it is never lower than the invoice.

Counts and recent activity for the account, in one call.

Totals for documents, customers and business profiles, a breakdown of
documents by status, and the ten most recent documents — cheaper than
paging each collection to build a dashboard.

The `invoice`-prefixed fields cover every document type, not only
invoices.

Recent API requests made with your keys, newest first.

Method, path, status, duration and the request and response bodies, so you
can see what an integration actually sent rather than what it meant to.

Filter to `success` or `error` with `status`. How long these are kept
depends on the plan — `get_usage_limits` reports the retention.

The numbering schemes that produce document numbers, newest first.

Each names the document type it numbers, so invoices and credit notes can
run on separate counters.

post.description:
Define how a document type's numbers are built.

A prefix, an optional date pattern, and a zero-padded counter — `INV-2026-0001`.
`reset` decides whether the counter returns to one each year.

get.description: One numbering sequence, including the number it will issue next.

patch.description:
Change a numbering scheme.

Numbers already issued are not rewritten, so a change takes effect from the
next document. Moving the counter backwards can collide with a number already
used.

delete.description:
Remove a numbering scheme.

Documents of that type then need their number supplied explicitly.

post.description:
Show the next number **without consuming it**.

Nothing is claimed, so calling this twice returns the same number and the
number stays available. Use `consume_sequence_number` to take it.
Consume and return the next number, incrementing the counter.

get.description:
Named tax rates you can apply by reference, newest first.

A convenience, not a requirement: a line item can state its rate inline
instead. Storing one means a rate change is made in a single place.

post.description:
Store a reusable tax rate.

`inclusive` decides whether the rate is already inside the unit price or
added to it — the difference is the total, so it is worth being sure. The
tax `category` travels with the rate into e-invoicing XML.

get.description: One stored tax rate.

patch.description:
Change a stored tax rate.

Documents already issued keep the rate they were calculated with. This
affects future documents only.

delete.description: Remove a stored tax rate. Documents already issued are unaffected.

get.description:
This account's jobs, newest first.

Without it the other three routes here were unreachable: a job id was never
returned by anything, so there was no way to arrive at one.
One job's status and progress.

post.description: Stop a job that has not finished.

Return a `failed` or `cancelled` job to `queued`, clearing its progress and error.

`409` from any other status.

Upload rows to be turned into documents, for review first.

Nothing is created yet: the rows are parsed and held so you can check them.
`confirm_import` commits them, `cancel_import` discards them.

get.description: An import's status and how many rows it holds.

post.description:
Commit a reviewed import, creating its documents.

Only from `pending` — an import already confirmed or cancelled returns `409`.
Discard an import without creating anything. Only while it is `pending` or `processing`.

get.description:
The currency codes a document may be issued in.

ISO 4217, with the minor-unit count each one uses — the amounts in this API
are integers in the currency's smallest unit, so that figure is what says
where the decimal point goes.

The country codes accepted anywhere an address is given.

ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

The locale codes accepted on a document or business profile.

The value is stored and returned as given; it is not currently applied to
anything a render produces.

The time zone names accepted on a business profile.

IANA names. Stored and returned as given: recurring schedules are evaluated
in UTC and do not consult it.
The page sizes a render can use.

UNCL5305, in full — the VAT treatment of a line, which its rate does not say.

Two lines at 0% may be zero-rated, exempt, reverse-charge or outside scope,
and EN 16931 puts them in separate VAT breakdown groups with different
mandatory fields. Exhaustive: a category outside this list is wrong.

UNCL5153 — which tax regime a document is issued under, one per document.

`VAT` is the only member an e-invoice can carry; the others exist so a
caller can state that their tax is *not* VAT and be told so, rather than
have VAT assumed on their behalf. There is no default: a PDF does not need
a scheme, and guessing one puts a claim in a document a tax authority reads
that the caller never made.

UN/ECE Recommendation 20 — the unit a line item is measured in.

A **shortlist**: twenty-one of hundreds, ordered by how often an invoice
needs them. `exhaustive` is false, and it means it — `unit_code` accepts any
value, nothing validates against this list, and an uncommon code is still
correct. Offered because the field takes a code rather than the printed
label: mapping "hrs" to HUR is an inference that is right until it silently
is not, and the audience for the result is a tax authority.

List every supported document type with the metadata a client needs to
build a type-aware create form: the number prefix, whether it is payable /
takes a source document / supports a reason, which line-item shape it uses
(``standard`` = priced, ``shipped`` = quantities only), and the lifecycle
actions available to it.
Workspaces this account owns, newest first.

post.description:
Create a workspace, owned by this account.

The creating account is added as its first member with the `owner` role.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retrying safe: a repeat with the
same key and body returns the original workspace instead of a second one.

get.description: One workspace by id.

patch.description:
Rename a workspace.

Only the fields you send are changed.

delete.description:
Delete a workspace and its membership list.

Every member record goes with it. This cannot be undone, and documents are
unaffected — they belong to the account, not the workspace.

get.description: Everyone on a workspace, with their role.

post.description:
Add someone to a workspace by email address.

Refused with 409 if that email is already a member. The address does not
have to belong to an existing account.

delete.description:
Remove someone from a workspace.

Removes the membership only; nothing they created is affected.

get.description: Every webhook endpoint registered on the account, newest first.

post.description:
Register a URL to receive events.

The endpoint starts active and begins receiving the events you list.

The response carries the signing secret, and is the only one that ever
will — store it now. Reading or listing endpoints never returns it, and
the only way to get another is `rotate_webhook_secret`, which stops this
one working.

get.description: One webhook endpoint by id.

patch.description:
Change an endpoint's URL, description, event list or active flag.

Only the fields you send are changed. Setting `is_active` to false stops
new deliveries while keeping the endpoint and its history, which is the
reversible alternative to deleting it.

delete.description:
Remove an endpoint and its delivery history.

The endpoint's delivery records are deleted with it, including any still
waiting to be retried. To stop deliveries without losing the history, set
`is_active` to false instead.

post.description:
Issue a new signing secret and return it.

This is the only response that contains the secret, so it is also how you
obtain the first one after creating an endpoint. The previous secret stops
being accepted immediately: signatures computed with it will not verify.

Send a test event to this endpoint.

Delivers a `test` event immediately, so you can confirm the URL is
reachable and your signature check works before real events depend on it.

Returns straight away with the delivery in `pending`; follow it with
`get_webhook_delivery` to see whether it arrived.

get.description:
Every webhook delivery attempt on the account, newest first.

One row per attempt to POST an event to one of your endpoints, with the
HTTP status and attempt count. For emails sent to your customers, see
`get_delivery`.

One webhook delivery by id — an HTTP POST to one of your endpoints.

Not to be confused with `get_delivery`, which is an email sent to a
customer.

post.description:
Send a failed or pending webhook delivery again, immediately.

Resets the attempt counter on the same delivery and dispatches it without
waiting for the retry schedule. Failed deliveries are already retried
automatically with backoff, so this is for after those are exhausted — or
to send a delivery created by `test_webhook_endpoint`.

Refused with 409 in any other status. To re-send an email, use
`retry_delivery`.

get.description: Get current subscription status (from DB, no Stripe API call).
Purchasable plans — the ones wired to a Stripe price.

patch.description:
Turn overage billing on or off for this account.

Off by default and stays off until asked: past the quota the API returns
429, which is a limit the customer can see coming. Overage replaces that
limit with a charge, and nobody should meet that decision on an invoice.

Create a Stripe Customer Portal session for self-service management.

standard.title: Standard
standard.description: The code list these values come from.

exhaustive.title: Exhaustive
exhaustive.description: Whether `data` is the complete list. When false it is a shortlist and other codes remain valid.

CodeListResponse.title: CodeListResponse
CodeListResponse.description:
A coded list from a standard, and whether it is the whole of one.

`exhaustive` is the field that changes what a client does. `true` means a
value outside `data` is wrong, so the list can back a picker with no escape
hatch. `false` means `data` is a shortlist of the codes an invoice usually
needs — the API accepts any code, nothing validates against this, and
treating it as closed rejects values that are perfectly valid.

ruleset_version.title: Ruleset Version
ruleset_version.description: The version these rules came from. Worth recording alongside any document you file — rulesets revise, and 'which rules did this pass?' is what an audit asks years later. `rulesets` breaks the same answer down per ruleset.

valid.title: Valid
valid.description: Nothing fatal was found. Read it with `fully_checked` — on its own it says what was checked came back clean, not that everything was checked.

in_scope.title: In Scope
in_scope.description: Whether any of these rulesets is likely to apply to this document at all. False when neither party is in a country that uses one — these are European e-invoicing rulesets, and for a wholly domestic US invoice, say, `valid` is answering a question nobody asked. Advisory: it never changes the verdict or withholds the check, because an open network means a US seller invoicing a Dutch buyer genuinely needs it.

fully_checked.title: Fully Checked
fully_checked.description: Every ruleset that applies to this profile ran. False means at least one could not, and `rulesets` says which and why.

rulesets.title: Rulesets
rulesets.description: Every ruleset the document was held to, including the mandatory-field check, at the version that ran.

violations.title: Violations
violations.description: Every violation found, not the first — fixing one field per round trip is the experience this avoids. Ordered mandatory-field findings first, since those name a field you can go and change.

version.title: Version
version.description: The upstream release of the rules. Empty for checks with no version of their own.

ran.title: Ran
ran.description: False when this ruleset could not be run at all. A ruleset that did not run is not a pass — `valid` only reports what was checked.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it did not run, when it did not.

ComplianceRulesetOut.title: ComplianceRulesetOut
ComplianceRulesetOut.description: One ruleset the document was held to, and whether it actually ran.

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: The identifier the standard uses — a business term from the mandatory-field check, a rule id from Schematron. A rule id is what a rejection notice from an access point quotes.

path.title: Path
path.description: Where the problem is. The mandatory-field check names a field of the request; Schematron names the node in the generated XML.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: `fatal` would get the document rejected. `warning` is a recommendation — both EN 16931 and Peppol grade a large share of their rules as advisory, and `valid` ignores those.

ruleset.title: Ruleset
ruleset.description: Which ruleset found it — matches an `id` in `rulesets`.

Email delivery. `sent` is terminal success — nothing reports back what
the provider did with the message after we handed it over.

profile.description: Which ruleset to hold the document to. Rulesets differ: a document valid under one can be rejected by another, so there is no default.

buyer_reference.title: Buyer Reference
buyer_reference.description: BT-10. Mandatory in Peppol BIS unless an order reference is present — often the buyer's own PO or cost-centre string.

tax_scheme.title: Tax Scheme
tax_scheme.description: UNCL5153 — what kind of tax this invoice states. One document, one answer: an invoice is issued under a tax regime, not a different one per line. Optional, and deliberately not defaulted, because a PDF does not need it and assuming `VAT` would put a claim in a tax document that you did not make. Required to produce or check an e-invoice, where it must be `VAT` — every ruleset built on EN 16931 describes VAT and tests for that string literally, so a document stating anything else is refused rather than relabelled.

delivery_date.title: Delivery Date
delivery_date.description: BT-72. When the goods or services were actually supplied — not the issue date, and what decides the VAT period. XRechnung requires this, an invoicing period, or a period on every line.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: `sync` renders inside the request and answers with the finished document. `async` returns `202` with a `queued` render a worker picks up; follow it with `GET /renders/{id}`. Use it for bursts — rendering is CPU-bound, so a hundred at once queue behind each other whichever mode you ask for, and only one of the two holds a connection open while they do.

expires_in.title: Expires In
expires_in.description: How long the render stays downloadable, in seconds (1 minute to 7 days). It is also the lifetime of the signature in `download_url`, which is why it is bounded: an unbounded value meant an unbounded grant. A value below the floor used to be accepted and produced a render that had already expired.

authority rather than a mailbox on a network.

NumberingNextOut.title: NumberingNextOut
NumberingNextOut.description:
What POST /numbering-sequences/{id}/next allocated.

The number is the point of the call. It used to answer with the sequence
row instead, so a caller burned a number and had to reconstruct the string
itself from prefix, date pattern and padding — the one thing the endpoint
exists to do for them.

frequency.description: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly

numbering_sequence_id.title: Numbering Sequence Id
numbering_sequence_id.description: Auto-generate invoice numbers from this sequence

RecurringInvoiceStatus.title: RecurringInvoiceStatus
RecurringInvoiceStatus.description:
Where a recurring schedule is in its life.

`completed` is the schedule running out, not a failure: it is set
automatically once the end date or the occurrence count is reached.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: The ruleset this document was built and validated against.

ruleset_version.title: Ruleset Version
ruleset_version.description: The artefact versions the check actually ran. A profile is held to more than one ruleset, and they are regenerated over time, so this is what makes 'which rules did this pass?' answerable later.

fully_checked.title: Fully Checked
fully_checked.description: False when a ruleset could not run. The document still satisfied everything that did, but the authoritative Schematron tier being absent is a materially weaker statement than it passing.

advisories.title: Advisories
advisories.description: Non-fatal findings the render proceeded past. Both rulesets grade a large share of their rules as advisory, so these are worth reading and are not a rejection.

RenderComplianceOut.title: RenderComplianceOut
RenderComplianceOut.description:
What this PDF was held to, for a render that carries embedded XML.

Absent on a plain `pdf`: no ruleset was applied, so there is no claim to
report. A render that was produced at all satisfied every fatal rule that
ran — the render is refused otherwise — so the useful questions are which
rules those were, and whether all of them ran.

code.title: Code
code.description: `compliance_failed` for a document that is well-formed and would be rejected by the ruleset it asked for; `unprocessable_entity` for one the renderer could not make sense of. The same codes the synchronous path returns.

details.title: Details
details.description: For `compliance_failed`: the profile, the ruleset version, and every violation with its rule, path, message and severity.

RenderFailureOut.title: RenderFailureOut
RenderFailureOut.description:
Why a render failed, in the same shape the synchronous path returns.

A synchronous render of a document EN 16931 would reject answers `422
compliance_failed` with every violation at once — a list of fields to go and
fill in. A queued render has to be able to say the same thing: the caller
who chose `async` did not choose a worse answer.

StandardLineItemInput.title: StandardLineItemInput
StandardLineItemInput.description: A fully priced line: unit, price, tax, discount and SKU.

code.title: Code
code.description: UNCL5305 tax category code — S standard, Z zero-rated, E exempt, AE reverse charge, K intra-community, G export, O outside scope

exemption_reason.title: Exemption Reason
exemption_reason.description: Required by EN 16931 whenever the category is not standard.

TaxCategory.title: TaxCategory
TaxCategory.description:
How a tax is treated, as opposed to what it is called.

`name` and `rate` do not say this: two taxes at 0% may be zero-rated,
exempt, reverse-charge or outside scope, and EN 16931 keeps them in
separate VAT breakdown groups with different mandatory fields. Optional,
so an invoice that never mentions a category calculates exactly as before.

category.description: Default treatment for this rate. A line item may override it.

TemplateConfig.title: TemplateConfig
TemplateConfig.description:
What a custom template is: a built-in design plus the brand to render it in.

A custom template is not a design of its own — it names one of the built-ins
in ``base_template_id`` and carries the values below, which are the same ones
``data.branding`` carries. They are applied *underneath* a request's own
branding, so a document that states a colour still wins and one template can
serve several brands.

Typed rather than the free-form object it used to be: nothing read that
object, so every key in it was equally correct and a caller could keep
sending ``primary_colour`` forever without a word back. Unset here means
"the template has no opinion" — unlike ``Branding``, whose every field has a
non-empty default and so cannot say that.

UsageOverage.title: UsageOverage
UsageOverage.description: Renders past the quota this period, and what they cost.

WebhookEndpointCreatedOut.title: WebhookEndpointCreatedOut
WebhookEndpointCreatedOut.description:
A newly created endpoint, including its signing secret.

The only time the secret is returned. Store it now: reading or listing
endpoints never includes it, and the only way to obtain another is to
rotate, which invalidates this one.

status.description: HTTP status, mirroring the response status line.

request_id.description: Trace id for this request; also returned as X-Trace-Id.
